authors.bio: Leslie Germany has been involved in the design of television cameras with the Pye company since 1946, and was first introduced to American television broadcasting through General Precision Laboratories in the early 1950's. He is a member of the SMPTE and BKSTS, a Fellow of the Royal Television Society, and is Technical Consultant with Pye TVT Ltd, Cambridge, England.
authors.name: L. W. Germany

authors.affiliation: N. V. Philips Gloeilampenfabrieken, the Netherlands
authors.bio: Henk Breimer studied Electronics at the Delft Technical University. In 1956, he joined the Philips Research Laboratories, where he worked on color TV receiver technology. In 1964 he transferred to the Philips-ELA Division to work on the Plumbicon color camera. Since 1972, he has been head of the Camera Development Laboratory.
authors.name: H. Breimer

authors.affiliation: N. V. Philips Gloeilampenfabrieken, the Netherlands
authors.bio: Henk Blom was born in 1936, and finished his studies at the Delft Technical University in 1966. He joined Philips in that year, where he worked in professional audio tape recording. Since 1968 he has been in the Professional Video Equipment division designing studio color television cameras.
authors.name: H. Blom

authors.affiliation: N. V. Philips Gloeilampenfabrieken, the Netherlands
authors.bio: Engbert Tienkamp was born in Kuiure the Netherlands, and received a teaching degree in physics and chemistry at the University of Groningen. He joined N. V. Philips Gloeilampenfabrieken in 1962 where he became involved in the environmental protection of industrial television equipment. Since 1964, he has been with the professional television division responsible for the design of the optical and colorimetric aspects of color television equipment. The current emphasis of his work is in optics and software system design.
authors.name: E. Tienkamp
